substitutions.from:
/* One card per court (data-court), same per-item loop pattern as the
   Waiting Room list -- replaces the old singleton teamAPlayers/teamBPlayers/
   scoreA/scoreB/qServeFirstRow/qTimerWrapper/liveScoreBtn/submitScoreBtn ids
   with one full set of controls per court slot: `_<court>`-suffixed ids, a
   `data-court` attribute on every per-court control, and its own listeners.
   Each court's score entry, live-score button, serve-first toggle, and
   (for Timed Rotation) timer are fully independent of every other court's.
   `affectedCourts`, when given, redraws only those specific court cards
   (replacing each one's existing DOM node in place) instead of wiping and
   rebuilding every card -- so a single-court action never touches any
   OTHER court's still-unsubmitted score inputs. */
substitutions.to:
/* Match-number colour coding for the dashboard's own court cards: same
   palette/cycle as queue.html (QueueEngine.matchColor keyed to the match
   NUMBER, not the court slot), just mapped to literal hex here instead of
   CSS variables -- this card (bg-[#201C19], see queueDashboard above) is a
   fixed dark panel regardless of the page's own light/dark theme toggle
   (bg-[#201C19] only ever remaps to the equally-dark --panel in dark mode,
   per theme.css), so one dark-friendly hex per colour is enough; no
   separate light-mode variant needed the way queue.html needs one for its
   own light cards. Values are the same pastel tones queue.html's own dark
   theme uses for blue/coral/green/amber/purple/teal (see its --match-*
   dark overrides), so both pages render the SAME colour per match number. */
const MATCH_COLOR_HEX = {
  blue:   { text: '#93C5FD', bg: 'rgba(147,197,253,.16)' },
  coral:  { text: '#FFB4AB', bg: 'rgba(255,180,171,.16)' },
  green:  { text: '#5AEF82', bg: 'rgba(90,239,130,.14)' },
  amber:  { text: '#FCD34D', bg: 'rgba(252,211,77,.16)' },
  purple: { text: '#CFC4FF', bg: 'rgba(207,196,255,.16)' },
  teal:   { text: '#5EEAD4', bg: 'rgba(94,234,212,.16)' },
};
